one_liner: Single-header C++17 constrained Delaunay triangulator with exact predicates; about 1.5-3x faster than CDT on polygon outlines, close to Triangle.
what_it_does: detria triangulates 2-D point sets (Delaunay or any valid triangulation) and polygons with multiple outlines, nested holes, extra constrained edges and user-supplied Steiner points. You build a detria::Triangulation, pass a point array and index polylines (addOutline, addHole, addPolylineAutoDetectType, setConstrainedEdge), call triangulate(delaunay), then iterate interior, hole or convex-hull triangles with callbacks. It is templated on point type (float, double or integer, any type with x/y or a point-getter), index type, allocator, container and sorter. A C# single-file port (Unity 2018+) is included.
how_it_is_fast: Points are sorted by x then y with a non-recursive quicksort, then inserted left to right in a sweep: each new point is joined to the visible part of the current convex hull, and Lawson edge flips restore the Delaunay property. Each constrained edge is inserted by walking the triangles it crosses, deleting them and re-triangulating the two cavity polygons on either side, followed by more flips. Inside/outside/hole classification is a pass over a compact half-edge topology. Shewchuk's adaptive robust orient2d and incircle predicates keep it exact without exact-arithmetic kernels.
when_to_use: Triangulating polygon outlines with holes from GIS or vector data (country borders, map tiles): detria beat CDT on 21 of 23 benchmark inputs (about 1.5-3.2x) and Triangle on all 13 country outlines by 4-30%
Replacing poly2tri: it was faster on all 14 inputs poly2tri could run (about 1.05-2.2x) and also handles multiple outlines, which poly2tri cannot
Projects that want a permissively licensed (MIT or WTFPL) drop-in single header instead of Triangle, whose license forbids commercial use without permission
Engines and tools that need exact results on degenerate input (collinear and cocircular points) and custom allocators or point types without copying data
C#/Unity projects that want the same algorithm via the bundled detria.cs port
when_not_to_use: Unconstrained Delaunay of large random point sets: Triangle was about 1.9x faster at 1,000,000 points (946 vs 1798 ms) and faster at every random-set size tested
Inputs with many cocircular points: on the depth-8 fractal detria took 3091 ms vs CDT 1407 ms and Triangle 857 ms
Mesh generation needing refinement, quality constraints, conforming Delaunay or automatic Steiner insertion: adding new points is a stated non-goal

Dirty input with intersecting or overlapping constraint edges, or points lying exactly on a constraint: triangulate() fails (ConstrainedEdgeIntersection, PointOnConstrainedEdge) instead of splitting edges, and duplicate points are also an error
Workloads needing incremental updates (insert or remove points after triangulation) or multi-threaded construction: neither is offered

integration.dependencies: none (C++ standard library only); Shewchuk's public-domain robust predicates are embedded
integration.min_toolchain: C++17 (C++20 for the module build; the repo's CMake asks for 3.30 but only the tests and benchmarks need it)
integration.platforms: any (portable C++; the benchmarks ran on Windows with clang-cl, the repo has Linux compile-test scripts, and an Emscripten build path exists for the benchmark)
integration.thread_safety: Documented: no global state, so separate Triangulation objects can run on separate threads; one object allows many concurrent const calls or exactly one mutating call (e.g. triangulate).

gotchas: setPoints and addOutline store pointers, not copies: the vectors must stay alive and unreallocated until triangulate() returns (DOCS.md shows both crash patterns)
Robust predicates break under -ffast-math or /fp:fast; the docs say to disable those flags. With integer coordinates, overflow is only checked in debug builds

Errors are reported by triangulate() returning false plus getError()/getErrorMessage(), not exceptions. Index and NaN checks can be disabled in the config, after which bad input is undefined behaviour
The default Idx is uint32_t, and the half-edge structure needs the edge count below half of Idx's maximum (e.g. 32767 edges with 16-bit indices)
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick detria for constrained triangulation of polygons with holes under a permissive license in one header. For plain point-set Delaunay, Delaunay32 (beats Triangle 1.6, CDT and Fade2D, multi-threaded) or Triangle itself are faster. pgl targets CGAL-style kernels with a broader geometry API.
verified_claims_summary: BENCHMARKS.md box plots (Clang 17.0.3 clang-cl, CMake Release defaults, Ryzen 9 3900X, Windows 10; CDT 58f34da, poly2tri 13d64e7, vendored Triangle with 'pzQ') time constrained triangulation of 13 Natural Earth outlines, poly2tri test files, cocircular fractals and random points. Medians: world land outline 502 ms vs CDT 1431 and Triangle 441; United States 24.4 vs 58.8 and 27.2; 1M random points 1798 vs Triangle 946. detria's timed region also includes copying out the result triangles, which the other three exclude, so this part is conservative against detria. The images were committed 2024-05-03, six days before a correctness fix (b15d5e2, 'last triangle around a constrained edge not always being delaunay'), so the published numbers predate that fix.
